entities.name: Distal findings vs proximal ASL
observations: In 1,910 average-risk screening colonoscopies, distal adenoma, hyperplastic polyp, or serrated polyp was not significantly associated with synchronous proximal advanced serrated lesions; ASL included dysplastic or ≥10 mm SSA/P and any traditional serrated adenoma. 52% of proximal ASL cases had no distal polyps.
Distal SSA/P was associated with any proximal SSA/P in secondary analysis (P=.008), but not established as associated with proximal advanced serrated lesions.

entities.name: Distal HP and later SSL
observations: A retrospective cohort found small (<10 mm) distal hyperplastic polyps associated with subsequent SSL versus normal index colonoscopy (OR 2.23, 95% CI 1.18–4.00); subsequent SSLs were not shown to meet advanced criteria.

entities.name: SSL location and metachronous risk
observations: A matched case-cohort study found increased metachronous advanced neoplasia associated with proximal and large SSLs, while distal SSLs were not associated with greater risk; outcome combined advanced adenomas and high-risk serrated lesions.
